significance: The sixth Tevaram shrine of the Kongu country, on the Kaveri at Kodumudi, sung by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar alike and bearing epigraphs of Pandya rulers including Maravarman Sundarapandian.
story: A crow is said to have tipped over sage Agastya's water-pot here, the spilt water flowing on as the Kaveri to nourish the farmlands downstream.
